                      Plate I · Statewide

                      About this atlas & its sources

                      Colors classify the origin or stated referent of each municipality’s current name. They stay the same as you explore earlier names and timeline records. Mixed or unresolved origins have their own category. Competing explanations remain part of each town’s name history.

                      In updated pilot towns, records keep source order and preserve qualified dates; the date overview does not imply a proportional time axis. Other towns retain the earlier edition’s dated overview. Numbered links open notes and sources for a particular name or event; each note has a link back. Records shared by multiple current towns are identified in their details.

                      Curated tours connect five stories around a theme. Connected histories explain a shared name, namesake, locality, or naming episode. Each town retains its own timeline and references.

                      This is an initial research edition. Disputed explanations and unconfirmed details are qualified where they appear.

                      Modern municipal and county boundaries come from the NJ Office of GIS municipal layer and county layer, retrieved September 11, 2026 and generalized for display. Surrounding land and the coastal display mask use the Census Bureau’s 2017 cartographic boundaries, distributed as U.S. Atlas 3.0.1. Municipal water territory is omitted from the colored display. Earlier governments and localities may have covered different areas.

                      Search covers town names, former names, namesakes, and names recorded in the timeline. A legend selection filters by current-name origin. The town menu offers the same selection as the map, including very small municipalities. Drag the map to pan; use the zoom buttons or choose a county for a closer view.

                      The town index offers an alphabetical way to browse the same stories. Search matches explain where a name appears. The compact name journey distinguishes local uses from municipal history; it does not imply that every name replaced the one before it. Town and event links reopen a particular story or timeline entry.

                      The map, research, and controls are included in this file and work offline. Source links open external websites and need an internet connection.
